content:
I’d like to thank everyone who develops and maintains Mathlib for Lean 4. Your work has made it possible for me to pursue a long-running hobby: exploring mathematical physics by formalizing, in Lean, what I encounter along the way.

I revisit and expand the code as the exploration develops. Over time, the project has grown from an attempt to formalize ideas around information geometry and a pregeometric, spinorial “prima materia” into a relatively dense graph of definitions, lemmas, and theorems spanning several fields. Its main thread is connecting ideas that are often treated as unrelated.

I also use the formalized code as a checkable context for reasoning and discussion with language models and coding agents. That has made Mathlib’s precise statements and reusable proofs especially valuable to me: they help keep speculative exploration anchored to definitions and verified results.

I’ve now opened the repository so that people and large-context coding agents can explore it freely. The project is still an evolving map of questions and connections, but I could not have built it without Mathlib and the work of its contributors.

Thank you for building and sharing such a remarkable library.
